messages:
michelle: Heads-up — escalated support ticket from Acme (large ARR) with three related API asks: streaming completions + function-calls, deterministic structured outputs, and an ask for stronger streaming guarantees. Putting this here for triage; customer is blocked by malformed fn_call payloads when using stream mode.

oliver: Ticket #89271 summary from support: when they enable stream=true and use functions, the function arguments arrive split across stream chunks and their broker rejects partial JSON. Example captured from their logs: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"stream\": true,
  \"functions\": [\"order.create\"],
  \"schema\": {\"orderId\": \"string\", \"items\": [ ... ] }
}
# emitted chunks we see:
{\"name\":\"order.create\",\"args\":\"{\\\"items\\\":[{\\\"id\\\":\\\"x\\\"}\"}\n{\"args\":\"{\\\"id\\\":\\\"y\\\"}]}\"}
```
They ask for either: (A) guarantee fn_call args are emitted atomically in the stream, OR (B) add an explicit `function_call_complete` event that contains the full args payload. They prefer (A) but will accept (B) if timeline is faster.

sam: Clarifying q: is this a protocol-level requirement or a runtime implementation detail? We currently stream token-level; atomic fn_call emission implies either server-side buffering until the function args are complete, or adding higher-level framing events. Buffering per-fncall could add latency/complexity.

nina: Triage context: severity=high (customer is blocked in prod), ARR ~ $1.1M, legal/regulatory nothing special. Suggested next steps: (1) classify as enterprise-blocking, (2) request perf budget estimate, (3) decide opt-in vs default change. Also confirm if Dedicated customers are already on a different runtime behavior.

alex: Technical note: streaming + structured schemas complicates things because many customers expect NDJSON style framing or an envelope. Two feasible approaches: 
- Envelope events: emit `event: function_call_start` / `event: function_call_chunk` / `event: function_call_complete` with complete JSON on complete event. (medium dev, low perf risk)
- Server-side atomic emission: buffer token stream until the fn_call args are fully assembled then emit as single atomic message in stream (simpler API, higher perf cost).

alex: My vote is to ship envelope events as default (minimal runtime change) and offer `stream_atomic_fncall=true` opt-in for customers who need single-chunk semantics.

michelle: :eyes: Can we scope a minimal, revertable change for Q2? Proposal: implement envelope events by default + docs + SDK examples, and make atomic buffering opt-in for a later follow-up. That gives the customer an immediate workaround and avoids surprising perf regressions.

sam: Rough estimates from runtime perspective: envelope events (API + spec + SDK samples) ~2w of dev + 1w QA. Server-side atomic buffering ~4w dev + perf benchmarking + infra testing. Need to run perf sims to quantify p99 changes.

oliver: Customer explicitly requested SDK guidance and prefers a flag-based opt-in if we do buffering. For now they'll accept envelope events if we provide clear migration guidance and an ETA.

nina: Action items: 1) michelle to confirm final ask + customer OK on envelope-events path and capture CL; 2) sam to run perf sim and return RPS/latency delta by EOW; 3) alex to draft framing/event spec & example payloads by next Tue; 4) support to notify customer with interim mitigation and ask for reproduction sample. I'll open a tracking GH issue.

ticket-bot: Created issue infra/89271-streaming-fncall-framing and linked to ticket #89271

michelle: Thanks all — I'm adding this to the backlog candidate list. @sam please mark as P0 candidate if perf looks acceptable after sims.

sam: Will do. :thumbsup:
